say.speaker: partner
say.text: Hold on, hold on! Do not blow the march horn yet, {name:lord}! My left crest feather is sticking straight up!

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Nobody at camp has touched the horn, {name:partner}. You have been staring into that water bucket for ten minutes.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Wind resistance matters when you lead the charge! One crooked tuft throws off my whole pivot.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Here, take the clean washcloth before you dump half our drinking water onto your head again.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Hey, I only spilled half a ladle yesterday! ...Wait. Is your pack strap twisted upside down again?

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Stand still a second. There! Straightened the buckle. Can't have our squad leader marching lopsided while I beat you to the ridge.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Race you to the trailhead, then. Last one past the signpost carries the heavy camp kettle tonight!

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Dinner call! Grab a seat by the fire, {name:lord}, before the stew cools off.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Wait a second. Why does my bowl have two extra berry dumplings while yours barely has broth?

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Huh? Must have been a clumsy ladle scoop! Besides, I was testing the spice earlier, so I am already half full.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: You said the exact same thing back home whenever Dad stretched winter rations. You used to slide half your supper onto my plate when I was looking away.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Well, somebody had to keep you fueled up! You always burned twice as much energy trying to climb orchard trees after dusk.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Fair enough, so here is my turn. Take one dumpling back right now, or I am eating half yours on tomorrow's lunch break.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Ha! Deal! Just don't complain when I still outrun you up the next hill on a lighter stomach!

say.speaker: lord
say.text: You are still awake, {name:partner}? Everyone else turned in an hour ago.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Couldn't sleep. Keep replaying that ambush earlier today, {name:lord}.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: We made it out without a single unit going down. What is eating at you?

say.speaker: partner
say.text: That third raider clipped your side when you jumped in front of me. You barely flinched, then kept barking orders like nothing happened.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Ever since Dad told us why he left the Royal Guard, I keep thinking about how fast a family can break if one person tries to absorb every hit alone.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: I didn't mean to scare you. I thought keeping a steady face would keep the squad calm.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Next time a blow actually stings, I will call it out right away. Promise. You shouldn't have to watch my back in the dark like this.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Good. Because if you hide a bruise again, I am dragging you straight to the medical tent myself.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Funny how quiet the camp looks right before sunrise. Almost reminds me of our old fence line back in the valley.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Except back then our biggest threat was getting caught stealing warm rolls off the cooling rack.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Hey, we pulled off some legendary heists on that cooling rack! Nobody else could have covered my exit like you did.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: We did not share the same egg, {name:lord}, and half the time we still argue over who takes point. Yet every road we walk feels like home as long as you are beside me.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Same here, {name:partner}. Whatever mysteries wait past the next kingdom, I want you at my side when we face them.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Then let us make it official right here. Sworn partners through every battle, every blizzard, and every absurd detour.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Shoulder to shoulder until the whole world is safe again. And maybe one day, a quiet supper back home.

say.speaker: partner
say.text: Deal! First one back to the homestead sets the table, and this time I am letting you take the bigger roll!

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Not one step past this log, {name:lord}. Drink this while it is still warm.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Whoa, {name:healer}! How did you even spot me behind the supply wagon?

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Because you always favor your left side when you are hiding a scrape. Let me see that bruise before you wave me off.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: It is barely a sting. Save the pecha salve for the scouts who actually took heavy hits today.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Chamomile and dried mint grow on every hillside, so you are not depriving anyone by sitting down for three minutes.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Oof, bitter! You definitely put extra root in this batch on purpose.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Consider it a gentle reminder to report to the healer tent before sneaking off next time!

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Those little white blossoms in your satchel look familiar, {name:healer}. Did we pass a patch like that on the road?

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Good eye, {name:lord}! I pressed these back in the orchard behind our homes the morning before we marched out.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: No wonder your bandages always smell like clean meadow air instead of camp smoke.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Steeped petals calm shaken nerves faster than any lecture. When battles get loud, scent brings people back to themselves.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Truthfully, seeing you steady out there on the field does that for me too. Knowing you are watching everyone's vitals keeps my head clear.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Oh! Careful, or you will make me drop my thread. Here, tuck this tiny woven sprig into your supply pouch.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Show me which dried leaves stop bleeding too, so I can carry a spare bundle when we split up on big maps.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Hold on, {name:healer}. Set that kettle down before you scald yourself. Your hands are shaking.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Ah... sorry, {name:lord}. Just tired from brewing extra tonic after that rough fight.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Sit on the crate and let me pour. You patched up the entire vanguard today without taking one break.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Whenever you sprint ahead to draw enemy fire, my heart jumps into my throat. Out in the valley, the worst injury was a scraped knee.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Now I watch you step into real ambushes, and I keep thinking what would happen if I reached you one second too late.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: I never stopped to think how heavy that watch is on you. I just wanted everyone behind me to stay safe.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: I will stop charging ahead without checking our spacing first. And when you are running on empty, you let me cover your rest.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Thank you, {name:lord}. Even healers need someone looking out for them now and then.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Look at the wildflowers blooming by the tent pegs, {name:lord}. Even trampled soil finds a way back to green.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Reminders of home always seem to sprout wherever you set up camp, {name:healer}.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Here. I braided an evergreen sprig into this flower charm so it will not wilt through snow or mountain wind.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: We have walked every mile from the orchard trail to the front lines together. I do not think I could lead this expedition without your voice keeping us grounded.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: And I found my courage because you never once turned away from someone in trouble. You shield our path, and I keep every heart whole.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Then let us bind that promise to this charm. Wherever the road takes us, through every storm and quiet season after, we stay anchored side by side.

say.speaker: healer
say.text: Lifelong companions, {name:lord}. And when peace finally settles, you owe me a whole afternoon of tea in the orchard!

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Even the bitter chamomile batch? Deal. I will drink every drop.

say.speaker: mentor
say.text: Rise and shine, {name:lord}! Dawn mist is lifting, which means twenty paces of guard rhythm before breakfast!

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Ugh... Dad, the sun isn't even over the treeline yet. Why am I the only one out here in the cold?

say.speaker: mentor
say.text: Haha! Because the squad looks to you when an ambush hits at first light! Now steady your stance and pivot cleanly on three.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Right... one, two, turn. Wait, why are you making me balance my supply pack while turning?

say.speaker: mentor
say.text: An unbalanced pack drags your blind side wide open. Good! Look at how crisp that pivot was compared to last week.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Wait, was that an actual compliment, or are you about to double the drill count?

say.speaker: mentor
say.text: Both! Ten more paces, champ, then I am flipping sweet-berry pancakes for everyone!

say.speaker: lord
say.text: What is that wooden medallion you are polishing by the coals, Dad? I have never seen you wear it.

say.speaker: mentor
say.text: Oh, this old thing? Just my Royal Guard cloak clasp. Thought I would scrub off the road dust before it turns green.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: You kept it tucked inside your saddlebag all those years in the valley, right under the spare aprons.

say.speaker: mentor
say.text: Ha... sharp eyes, {name:lord}. Back when I hung up my royal cloak, I swore I would trade palace halls for burnt stewpots and quiet mornings.

say.speaker: mentor
say.text: Sometimes I still wonder if hiding in that orchard made me soft, or if bringing you kids onto real roads broke the only promise I kept right.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Those years taught us how to look after neighbors, share rations, and hold our nerve under pressure. Nothing about that life was wasted, Dad.

say.speaker: mentor
say.text: You sure know how to talk sense into an old guard. Keep that fire burning strong, kid.

say.speaker: mentor
say.text: Look at these scouting notes on the ridge ambush. Stay behind my line tomorrow, {name:lord}, while I draw the heavy hitters first.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: If you sprint into the ravine alone, archers on the bluff will box you in. Let me anchor the western brush while our ranged units clear the ledge.

say.speaker: mentor
say.text: Wait... you already mapped the crossfire angles from the ridge? When did you learn to read terrain like a captain?

say.speaker: lord
say.text: You have been drilling formation spacing into us since we were knee-high, Dad.

say.speaker: mentor
say.text: Truth is, I kept stepping in front of you because I was terrified of failing to shield you the way I promised myself I always would.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: You do not have to shoulder the whole front line by yourself anymore. Let us guard your flank for a change.

say.speaker: mentor
say.text: Heh... look at me getting misty-eyed over a map board. All right, Commander {name:lord}.

say.speaker: mentor
say.text: Tomorrow we take that ravine together, side by side. Lead the march.

say.speaker: combee
say.text: Oh! Careful, careful! Excuse us, {name:lord}, we brought dry kindling for the camp stove... sorry we dropped two sticks!

say.speaker: lord
say.text: No harm done, {name:combee}. Looks like one of you is nodding off mid-hover though.

say.speaker: combee
say.text: Yes, our bottom one drifted right out after hauling three pails of water. Top left watches east, top right watches west, and bottom usually keeps count... Zzz...

say.speaker: combee
say.text: Whoa! Sorry! Bottom is awake now! Wait, did we already hand over the firewood?

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Set the bundle by the hearth and take a real breather. Nobody can fly guard shift on zero sleep.

say.speaker: combee
say.text: We promise we are much sharper in battle! The Queen expects swift wingwork, and we want to earn our keep beside you!

say.speaker: lord
say.text: You already proved your nerve at the spring. Grab some dinner and rest all six wings tonight.

say.speaker: combee
say.text: Pardon us, {name:lord}! We saved a little sealed jar of clover honey from our hive pouch just for you!

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Clover honey? Isn't that emergency trail food from your own hive stores, {name:combee}?

say.speaker: combee
say.text: Squad leaders burn the most stamina keeping everyone moving! Besides, the bottom one already licked the spoon clean... wait, no I didn't!

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Wait a second. Did you three skip lunch while out foraging nectar for the rest of the camp?

say.speaker: combee
say.text: Well, everyone else here grew up together or trained like knights. We just wanted to make sure nobody minded having humble scouts around.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: You helped us clear outlaws off our own watering hole. Sit down right now and pass two spare spoons over here.

say.speaker: combee
say.text: Yay! Three spoons for three bees, wait, four with yours! Sweetest break we have had all week!

say.speaker: combee
say.text: Whew! Did we swoop across the eastern ridge fast enough, {name:lord}? Our bottom half nearly clipped a pine branch on the turn!

say.speaker: lord
say.text: You cut off that entire flanking squad before they could touch our rear line. Without you three in the air, we would have been boxed in.

say.speaker: combee
say.text: Really? Even the bottom bee stayed wide awake through the whole dive!

say.speaker: combee
say.text: I did! I spotted the second raider hiding behind the boulder and yelled first!

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Ha! Looks like all three of you are running in perfect sync now, {name:combee}.

say.speaker: combee
say.text: When we flew down to that watering hole, we only hoped for a few pails to bring the Queen.

say.speaker: combee
say.text: Instead we found a crew worth flying through storms for. Wherever you point us, {name:lord}, all three of us are right behind you!

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Glad to have you in our core vanguard. Keep those eyes sharp on the horizon!

say.speaker: chespin
say.text: Hup! Step, brace, hold! One hundred paces down, one hundred more to go!

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Are those river boulders strapped inside your pack, {name:chespin}? We already finished marching for the day!

say.speaker: chespin
say.text: Commander {name:lord}! My thanks for the concern, yet a squire of modest foot speed must forge endurance twice as hard.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: You held that foothill choke point against four raiders without yielding an inch. Nobody here doubts your stamina.

say.speaker: chespin
say.text: Holding steady ground is the barest duty of a shield-bearer. Until my armor outlasts every strike, my drills remain unfinished.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: At least take this waterskin and drop the rocks before supper gets cold. Even knights need fuel for tomorrow's wall.

say.speaker: chespin
say.text: My thanks, Commander. After you take your own meal first, I shall join you at the fire!

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Hold on, {name:chespin}. Why are you hammering dents out of your buckler by yourself instead of visiting the medical tent?

say.speaker: chespin
say.text: A knight does not trouble our healer over mere scuffs on gear, {name:lord}. Once I tighten this strap, I am fit for duty.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: That is not gear wear. Your guard arm has a deep bruise right under the buckle.

say.speaker: chespin
say.text: ...Forgive me. During the uphill pursuit today, the faster scouts outpaced me. I sprinted recklessly to catch up and took a flank blow unbraced.

say.speaker: chespin
say.text: If my legs cannot reach an ally in peril before steel falls, what worth is my shield?

say.speaker: lord
say.text: That is my fault as leader for letting the line stretch too thin. From now on, we anchor our advance around your pace.

say.speaker: chespin
say.text: You would slow the vanguard on my account? My thanks, {name:lord}... I swear I shall never let that wall break.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Wind is biting cold up on this ridge, {name:chespin}. Your watch shift ended twenty minutes ago.

say.speaker: chespin
say.text: A sentinel stays vigilant until dawn, {name:lord}. Besides, the quiet lets me think clearly.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: About what? You seem even quieter tonight than usual.

say.speaker: chespin
say.text: Back on the Foothill Trail, when those bandits surrounded me... I truly believed nobody would answer my call. I had made peace with falling on that path alone.

say.speaker: chespin
say.text: Yet you and your family charged straight into the fray without hesitation. I have been trying to repay that debt ever since.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: You already repaid us ten times over every time you stepped into harm's way for this squad. Stop thinking you owe us your life, {name:chespin}.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: True chivalry isn't dying alone on some hillside. It is living to stand shoulder to shoulder with allies who have your back.

say.speaker: chespin
say.text: ...I see. Then I shall guard my own life just as fiercely as yours. My thanks... my friend.

say.speaker: chespin
say.text: Commander {name:lord}! If I may have a solemn moment before the march sounds...

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Whoa, stand up, {name:chespin}! Why are you kneeling out here in the dew?

say.speaker: chespin
say.text: Once, I believed knightly honor meant swearing fealty to a distant throne and enduring every hardship alone.

say.speaker: chespin
say.text: Marching beside you showed me something far truer. Honor lives in the companions who trust you with their lives and never leave you behind.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Then rise and stand eye to eye with me, {name:chespin}. I don't want a retainer kneeling behind me; I want an equal partner beside me.

say.speaker: chespin
say.text: So be it! You be the spearhead that breaks the darkness, and I shall be the unyielding bastion at your flank.

say.speaker: lord
say.text: Sworn partners through every battle ahead, and steadfast friends long after the banners come down.

say.speaker: chespin
say.text: On my shield and my name, partner! Lead on, and I shall keep pace with you all the way!
